notes: Group totals and the RM270.10/t total are as printed in PA Table 23. Harvest items are per tonne as printed in Table 21 (they sum to 86.19 actual / 94.18 budget; Table 23 prints 86.18 / 94.19, rounding).

Upkeep and general-charge items are calc: RM amount (Tables 6 and 7) / 24,682.36 t actual or 23,680 t budget FFB (the bases Table 23 uses). Upkeep has 18 lines; the 13 largest by actual are shown and the rest summed as Other (Weeding - others, Drains, Boundaries/survey/fences, Supplying, Tools).
Upkeep lines in Table 7 add to RM2,518,883.26 vs the printed total RM2,518,021.43 (RM861.83 more), so items sum to about RM102.05/t vs the printed 102.02. Budget lines add exactly to RM3,596,640.

General charges: Table 23 charges only RM2,021,487 (budget RM2,191,813) of the full RM2,370,932 (budget RM2,584,836) in Table 6. The budget figure equals RM2,584,836 x 1,289.58/1,520.82 ha exactly, i.e. apportioned to the pre-replanting mature area; the actual is 85.3% of Table 6, a basis the report does not state (Appendix 1 line 'Proportionate of GC - mature' is blank). Item figures here are the full Table 6 amounts per tonne, so they sum to about RM96.06/t actual and RM109.16/t budget, above the printed group totals RM81.90 and RM92.56.
No dispatch, depreciation or head-office lines are given; RM270.10/t is ex-estate field cost.

Note Agro's diff % column divides by the new-year yield, so it understates gains: true changes are 1998 +38%, 2000 +25%, 2001 +5.3%, 2002 +1.0%, 2005 +2.7%, 2018 -7.2%, 2020 +41%, 2022 from 1.07 to 13.17 t/ha, estate +4.9%. Agro: yield up nearly 5%; P98 and P00 rose over 20% mainly because low-yield, low-density, Ganoderma blocks were removed by replanting; P00 still lowest and to be fully replanted FY2026/27; P01, P02, P05 satisfactory for age; P20 should exceed 22 t/ha in FY2026/27; P22 first harvesting year, will rise further; P18 near potential but needs thinning. Drought June-August 2025 may cause bunch abortion and fewer bunches about six months later. Caution: PA gives last year 14.84 t/ha, Agro 18.15 t/ha, and Agro table rows do not add to its totals (see issues).

HARVESTING (PA). Two mini tractors cover 892.18 ha; machine 34.60 t/day (text says 31.72), harvesters 3.53 t/man-day. Harvester output (Table 19): tall palms 2.35-2.85 t/man-day at RM31-38/t, RM90-100/day; young palms 1.25-1.53 t at RM65-100/t, RM99-109/day. Intervals 10-19 days, 24.10-29.00 rounds in 12 months (Table 20). Agro Table 7: P01, P02, P05 intervals fell from 17-19 days (May 2025) to 8-11 days (Apr 2026); no delays, no backlog; keep under 15 days.

COST OF PRODUCTION (PA Table 23, 12 months to April 2026, RM per tonne FFB, actual vs budget). General charges 81.90 vs 92.56 (RM2,021,487 vs 2,191,813). Upkeep and cultivation 102.02 vs 151.89 (RM2,518,021 vs 3,596,640). Harvesting and collection 86.18 vs 94.19 (RM2,127,098 vs 2,230,356). Total RM270.10/t vs RM338.63 (RM6,666,606 vs 8,018,809), 20% below budget, mainly from higher crop and lower upkeep and collection. Note the general charges in Table 23 are only about 85% of the RM2,370,932 in Table 6. The budget RM2,191,813 equals the full budget apportioned by the old mature area (1,289.58 of 1,520.82 ha); the basis for the actual is not stated. Charging the full general charges would give about RM284/t.

HARVEST AND COLLECTION COST (PA Table 21, RM/t actual vs budget). FFB supervision 6.28 vs 4.74; harvesting own FFB 41.62 vs 63.22; contract harvesting and collection 16.30 vs 3.09 (RM402,236 vs 73,080); loose fruit collection 2.51 vs 0.42; infield loading 10.22 vs 13.35; internal transport 8.33 vs 8.06; tools 0.93 vs 1.30. Total 86.19 vs 94.18 (RM2,127,099 vs 2,230,356).

GENERAL CHARGES (PA Table 6 and Appendix 1, 12 months, RM/ha planted). Staff salary and related RM777,977 (RM512/ha vs 582); labour overhead RM900,563 (592 vs 589); office and related RM658,773 (433 vs 507); office and premises upkeep RM33,553 (21 vs 22); misc RM65. Total RM2,370,932 vs RM2,584,836, RM1,558.98/ha vs RM1,699.63 (8% below). Overspends over 10%: staff welfare +RM7,773 (training, practical students); telecom +RM367; non-capitalised assets +RM2,745 (water heaters); office equipment +RM2,590 (printer toner).

UPKEEP AND CULTIVATION (PA Table 7, 12 months, RM/ha actual vs budget). Supervision 33 vs 57. Weeding 298 vs 286 (selective/blanket 188 vs 117, circle 102 vs 166, others 8 vs 3). Manuring 652 vs 1,374 (labour 43 vs 70, transport 31 vs 304, material 579 vs 1,000). Pests and diseases 198 vs 151 (bagworm 152 vs 53, rat baiting 22 vs 36, others 24 vs 62). Composting 479 vs 462. Census and thinning 20 vs 11. Drains 1 vs 50. Roads and bridges 89 vs 219. Boundaries 0 vs 16. Supplying 3 vs 0. Pruning 165 vs 161. Tools 5 vs 0. Total RM2,518,021.43 = RM1,942/ha vs RM3,596,640 = RM2,789/ha.

WEEDING. PA Tables 8 and 10 (12 months): circle 3,249.16 of 3,517.62 ha (92%, 2.77 rounds), all fields 3 rounds except 2001 at 2 (delayed on purpose); selective 3,457.00 ha (98%, 2.9 rounds). Extra selective cost from slashing woody growth along the Serting River and Stenochlaena. Young areas still have Clidemia, Asystasia, lalang and Giant Paspalum. Agro (March 2026): P01, P02, P05 two of three rounds done; Ageratum in parts of P02 circles. Agro Table 13 young mature: interrow P18 97%, P20 63%, P22 13%; circle P18 4%, P20 33%, P22 120%. Nephrolepis in P22 circles; dense grasses block evacuation in low-lying P20.

MANURING. PA Table 11 (FY2025/26): 893.82 of 1,019.17 mt applied (88%); only February NK Mix short (16.69 of 52.55 mt, 31%, supplier shortage), finished by the visit. Cost RM652/ha, 47% of budget (material RM579 vs 1,000). Agro Table 5 (March 2026): mature 1,461.61 mt applied vs 593.16 mt estimated (RP 845.90 vs 143.50), yet Agro lists many late or missed rounds: NK Mix in P01C/D, P02D/F/G and P05; Mix B five months late in P18/P20 with later rounds pending; P22A first Mix B round not done. Manager says manuring is up to date; Agro asks for accurate records.

FERTILISER PROGRAMME FY2026/27 (Agro Appendix 1, no revision; grams per palm). P01C/D NK Mix 2,500 g in May and Nov; P01A/B/E/F/G and P00C to be replanted, no manuring. P02 NK Mix 2,500 g in Jun, then 2,000-2,500 g in Oct and Feb (6,500-7,500 g a year; C, D, E higher). P05 MIX A 2,000 g in Jun, Sep, Dec and Mar = 8,000 g. P18 (AAR clone) Mix B 2,200 g in May, Aug, Nov, Feb plus RP 2,000 g in Sep = 10,800 g. P20A/B Mix B 2,000 g x4 plus RP 2,000 g = 10,000 g; P20C Mix B 1,700 g in May and Aug, 2,000 g in Nov and Feb, plus RP 2,000 g = 9,400 g. P22 Mix B 1,500 g (May), RP 2,000 g (Jul), Mix B 1,700 g in Aug, Nov, Feb = 8,600 g. PR2025A/D compound 800, 1,000, 1,200 g plus RP 1,500 g = 4,500 g; PR2025B/C compound 800 and 1,000 g plus RP 1,500 g = 3,300 g. Blocks listed as 2025 E/F/G (the PR2026 planting): compound 1,000, 1,200, 1,100-1,200, 1,300-1,500 g plus RP 1,700 g. New plantings CRF 600 g plus RP 500 g in the hole, then nothing for 9 months. Fertiliser to be calculated on the latest palm density.

COMPOSTING. PA Table 12 (12 months): mature 19,217.32 t on programme 12,847.10 t (150%), 14.96 t/ha; 2005 25.92 t/ha, 2002 21.23, 2001G 20.39, 2018 4.27, 2022 0.19, 2000C and 2020 nil, so still treated as delayed; immature 488.24 t unbudgeted. Cost RM479/ha vs RM462. Agro Table 6 (March 2026): 10,175.52 t on 774.89 ha; application now on hold because of high diesel prices; compost not sampled since 2025, so treat it as a supplement not a substitute for fertiliser.

PESTS AND DISEASES. Rats: PA Table 13 baiting with Storm (flocoumafen 0.05%) in 2018 and "2019" (means 2020), 184.72 ha, 7 and 8 rounds; RM22/ha. Barn owl boxes (PA Table 14) 142 vs 149 required, 1 per 11 ha, 22 occupied (15%), versus over 90% at neighbouring Bukit Jin Estate; cause to be investigated. Agro: random census found over 20% fresh damage in P18 and P22; no census in P22, irregular in P18/P20; one baiting round in P22 on 15 April 2026 with no replacement; systematic block-by-block baiting with 7-day replacement until acceptance below 20%. Estate census figures of 80-100% damage in P01/P02 called questionable; use platform census with 20% threshold in tall palms. PA says no serious rat attack. Bagworm: 2025 outbreak in P18 controlled with Dipel (67.91 ha treated, 4 rounds); bagworm RM152/ha, 186% over the RM53 budget; total pests and diseases RM198/ha vs 151. No reinfestation (both reports). Ganoderma: serious in old palms; mounding done in P05; no updated census since the previous visit (Agro); annual GPS census advised, half-yearly where over 5%.

PRUNING. PA Table 16: progressive pruning paid every 3 months, all rounds 100%; fronds stacked between 4 palms; slight over-pruning in young palms (2018B). Cost RM165/ha vs 161. Agro: P01, P02, P05 acceptable, keep one subtending frond; P18 and P20 up to date but over-pruning in P20 and fronds left in circles in P20B; P22 under-pruned with long frond butts and fronds in circles, must be completed.

YOUNG MATURE (Agro section 5). P22: stunted, pale palms on silty, compacted, waterlogged soil; leaf N 2.40%, P 0.153%, K 1.34%, Mg 0.27%, B 17.93 ppm, an uptake problem; advice scupper drains, compost or EFB 40 t/ha, subsoil manuring. P20: small palms on gravelly hills, mild K and Mg deficiency. P18 at 170 SPH needs hexagonal thinning. P05 low-lying areas pale, mild N and K deficiency on laterite P05D.

IMMATURE. PR2025 (129.66 ha, ex 1998A/B/E and 2000A): planted by June 2025 at 148 SPH after weather delays and a July 2024 seedling phytotoxicity incident; watermelon intercrop (grower has now stopped per PA); circles need weeding; first ablation done. PR2026A-C (101.58 ha): Agro Table 15 (April 2026) 12,921 of 15,034 palms planted (86%), land preparation delayed by the contractor; Mucuna only 40%, so keep soft grasses. PA (June) says planting completed, watermelon resumed on 50 ha, census needed. PR2026D-G (179.60 ha): felled and deboled, infilling under way; plant October-November 2026.

DRAINS, ROADS (PA). Drains RM1/ha; desilting needed in low-lying young mature area. Road grading budget RM20,184, nothing done; roads RM89/ha vs 219.

VEHICLES (PA Table 24). 10 farm and 12 mini tractors; WXG 4457 and 3 mini tractors unused, to be sold. Six farm tractors over budget per hour (worst BQD 3982 RM37.66 vs 11.10), mainly repairs from under-use.

RAINFALL (Agro Appendix 2, May-April years). FY21/22 3,080.93 mm, 112 days; FY22/23 2,456.19 mm, 113; FY23/24 2,858.05 mm, 108; FY24/25 2,991.79 mm, 161; FY25/26 May-March only 1,354.92 mm, 125 days (April blank); July 2025 only 8.4 mm.

CONCLUSIONS. PA: performance satisfactory; yield 19.04 t/ha and cost RM270.10/t both better than budget. Agro key issues: waterlogging in old and young mature areas; poor upkeep in P22; heavy rats in P18 and P22; circle weeding delays in PR25; PR26 replanting behind schedule.
